summary: Adds a discount_code field and an apply_discount method to Order. It also adds order detail and redeem endpoints.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any logged-in user
findings.problem: The order_detail view looks up the order by primary key only. It never checks that the order belongs to request.user.
findings.consequence: Any logged-in user can read the total and discount code of every order by iterating order ids.
findings.fix: Filter the lookup by owner=request.user, as the redeem view already does.

findings.title: Decimal multiplied by float raises TypeError
findings.problem: The total field holds a Decimal, and apply_discount multiplies it by the float 0.9. Python raises TypeError for Decimal times float.
findings.consequence: Every redeem request with the valid code fails with a server error. No user can ever apply the discount.
findings.fix: Multiply by Decimal("0.9") and quantize the result to two decimal places.

findings.title: New model field has no migration
findings.problem: The change adds discount_code to Order, but the change adds no migration. The only migration is 0001_initial, which has no discount_code column.
findings.consequence: Every Order query selects a column the database lacks. The order list, detail and redeem views then fail.
findings.fix: Run makemigrations for the orders app and commit the generated migration.

findings.title: CSRF protection disabled on session-authenticated POST
findings.problem: The redeem view changes order state for the session user, and the decorator turns off CSRF checks. The settings enable CsrfViewMiddleware, so the view opts out on purpose.
findings.consequence: Any third-party site can make a logged-in user's browser redeem codes on that user's orders.
findings.fix: Remove the csrf_exempt decorator and have clients send the CSRF token.

findings.title: New discount and view behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds apply_discount and two views, and the repository has no tests for them.
findings.consequence: Simple redeem and detail tests would have caught the float crash and the missing owner check.
findings.fix: Add tests for apply_discount, redeem, and order_detail, including access by a non-owner.
